transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-06-18 16:00 UTC | Duration: 46 minutes | Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Sofia Nguyen (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Redwood CSM), Maya Lopez (Acuity Eng Mgr), Rajesh Nair (Acuity DevOps), Elena Petrova (Acuity Sec), Tom Becker (Acuity ML)

Summary: Short sync to review last week's upgrade, investigate increased tail latency for long requests, confirm network routes for Private VPC pilot, and agree on next benchmark and security artefacts.

00:00 Jordan (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time. quick roll call, then i'll turn it over to sofia for the perf findings we ran Friday.
00:12 Maya (Acuity): hi, maya here. rajesh on audio, elena, tom, all good.
00:18 Rajesh (Acuity): hey all.
00:22 Sofia (Redwood): ok so quick context, after the 6-11 cluster agent update we saw a rise in p50 is fine but tail grows on long streaming calls, it's mostly visible beyond 4k token sessions. we suspect routing + kv cache interactions, so we did a few experiments.
00:41 Tom (Acuity): yeah we saw a couple of 5-6s stalls mid-stream which weren't present before.
00:48 Sofia: right, initial hypothesis is that the new kernel selection change plus our route between AZ-a and AZ-b causes extra cross-AZ hops for cache lookups, that adds 100-200ms per miss, and for long sessions the effect compounds.
01:10 Jordan: can you remind us which images you pushed and the helm values? i know you upgraded to image rdx-agent:2025-06-10-rc2, correct?
01:19 Tom: correct, and we also flipped the batcher to continuous mode in config which may change KV behavior.
01:27 Sofia: yep that's the one. continuous batching is fine but requires pinned socket affinity to avoid cross-node lookups. we added a short doc in the bench notes, link in the chat - bench/rdx-agent-upgrades.md.
01:40 Maya: we might have missed the affinity change when we rolled, that's on us.
01:45 Rajesh: i pulled traceroutes earlier, i can share but quick note: our route table didn't have the new /32 peering entry from redwood's transit VPC, so traffic was going via NAT in another AZ.
02:06 Jordan: that would explain it - cross-AZ NAT adds latency. ok rajesh can you paste traceroute so we can confirm?
02:13 Rajesh: yes, will drop the logs in the channel after.
02:17 Elena: also from security side, when you flipped the agent you saw some logs flagged by our IDS because of the new outbound port range. we need to confirm the approved egress set.
02:30 Jordan: understood, we'll include the exact port range and IPs in the peering doc.
02:35 Sofia: next i ran a controlled bench: 100 parallel 4k-token streams for 30 minutes. p50 ~ 130ms, p95 jumped from 450ms to 820ms after the upgrade. when i forced local KV hits by warming prefixes the p95 dropped to ~420ms, so cache misses are the primary contributor.
03:05 Tom: warming prefixes helped a lot in our dev env too. question: can we do smarter prefetch or do we need a stronger cache size?
03:15 Sofia: we recommend two short fixes: 1) KV cache tuning - increase in-memory shard size for your agent group and enable socket affinity; 2) fallback routing to avoid cross-AZ NAT for KV lookups by adding the /32 peering entry. long term we can add a prefetch heuristic but that's a code change.
03:39 Rajesh: increasing memory is doable but needs kernel tuning on our side; i'll need the exact JVM/native mem guidance.
03:48 Sofia: i'll put the memory knobs and commands in the JIRA ticket, plus a one-line script to patch the helm values.
03:56 Jordan: also practical note - if you want to avoid the risk we can temporarily route KV lookups to a Dedicated fallback in the same AZ; cost small for short trial.
04:08 Maya: what's the estimator for that cost? we have a tight budget.
04:12 Jordan: rough back-of-envelope for 2 weeks of dedicated fallback at minimal cluster is about $3k, but i'll send a formal estimate.
04:21 Elena: for the KMS question, we need to confirm whether redwood will rotate customer-managed keys or we manage rotation. also audit logs retention needs 13 months minimum.
04:34 Jordan: policy is customer manages CMKs, but we support auto-rotation if you opt in; i'll send the SOC2 packet and KMS integration map. retention 13 months is fine, we can confirm storage tier.
04:45 Sofia: small note on the upgrade process - the agent now supports staged rollouts by model route, so we can target only your internal test route first; that reduces blast radius. we used your test route for canary last week.
05:02 Tom: that would be useful. can we have a checklist to run before each rollout?
05:09 Sofia: yes i'll add a preflight checklist to the repo and link it.
05:15 Rajesh: i uploaded traceroutes, paste here we see hop 4 going to NAT-azb, which matches the missing route.
05:25 Jordan: thanks, that aligns. next step is you add the /32 entry, retest, and we'll run the 5k token bench.
05:33 Maya: timeline - rajesh can do route change tomorrow morning, we can run bench on Thursday.
05:39 Rajesh: confirmed.
05:43 Sofia: about the KV cache tuning, i'm going to open a ticket with steps: increase in-memory shards from 4 to 8, set socketAffinity=true, and set kvPrefetch=1 for now. that should reduce miss rate.
06:00 Tom: does prefetch 1 risk consistency issues?
06:04 Sofia: shouldn't, it's speculative prefetch of the next block; it's safe for inference workloads. we'll monitor.
06:12 Elena: on access controls, we need RBAC mapping for who can trigger model rollouts; we want only two of our admins to have that capability.
06:21 Jordan: yep we support RBAC via SAML groups; i'll include mapping docs and a sample SAML assertion for your IdP.
06:29 Elena: also, audit trail needs to show who triggered rollouts and what image was used.
06:36 Liam (Redwood CSM): we'll ensure rollout events are shipped to your audit log bucket with image and actor. i'll coordinate retention.
06:48 Maya: perfect.
06:52 Sofia: any other perf items? i also ran a quantization profile test; results showed no degradation for your workload when running 4-bit INT with the current model, so that's an option to lower memory pressure.
07:07 Tom: would quant help reduce tail latency?
07:10 Sofia: indirectly - lower memory footprint reduces swapping and more cache residency; it helps but not substitute for routing fixes.
07:19 Rajesh: can you share the quant profile creds or script? we need to reproduce.
07:25 Sofia: yes will push the profile and the reproduce script to the bench repo. link in notes.
07:32 Jordan: ok, to recap next steps: rajesh will update route table, run traceroute and bench; sofia will open KV tuning ticket and push helm patch; jordan will send security + pricing; elena to confirm KMS policy; tom to run quant reproducer. agreed?
07:51 Maya: agreed.
07:54 Jordan: any blockers besides the egress port/route?
07:58 Elena: once we have the exact egress ports from redwood, we can whitelist.
08:03 Jordan: i'll include ports 443 plus 15000-15005 for agent heartbeats and kv.
08:12 Rajesh: got it.
08:15 Sofia: one operational note - during the 6-11 upgrade we briefly hit an autoscaler flapping event because of a misconfigured probe; we added a stable probe in rc2 but please confirm readiness probe path /healthz in your helm values.
08:36 Tom: ah yes our probe path was still /ready, i'll change it.
08:40 Jordan: good catch.
08:42 Liam: i'll follow up on the onboarding checklist items and add the rollout dates to the playbook.
08:48 Maya: thanks liam.
08:50 Jordan: last thing - timeline for next sync? if rajesh runs routes tomorrow and bench on Thursday, let's meet next Monday same time to review numbers. does that work?
08:59 Maya: Monday works.
09:02 Rajesh: works for me.
09:05 Jordan: great. i'll send calendar invite and attach the SOC2 packet, helm patch, and the bench script.
09:12 Elena: thanks everyone.
09:15 Meeting end.

References and shared artifacts: bench/rdx-agent-upgrades.md (internal link), bench/5k-throughput-script.sh, repo/helm/rdx-agent-values-patches.yaml, security/soc2-snapshot.pdf, security/vpc-peering-checklist.md.

Action items (as discussed):
- Rajesh - add /32 peering route entry, share traceroute logs, run 5k-token bench by 2025-06-19.
- Sofia - open JIRA for KV cache tuning and push helm patch to bench repo by 2025-06-19.
- Jordan - send SOC2/ISO pack, KMS integration doc, and Dedicated fallback pricing estimate by 2025-06-19.
- Tom - run quantization reproducer and share results by 2025-06-25.

End transcript.
